subject: cardboardRobot
pitch:
Category: Humanoid character.
Subject: kid in a cardboard-box robot costume.
Style: cardboard craft.
reasoning:
I'm sketching the design for a kid-sized cardboard robot costume: a box torso and head with a face cutout, foil-wrapped limb tubes, buttons, dials, and an antenna, posed with arms slightly extended and legs apart.

Now I'm planning the skeleton structure, placing hips, spine, chest, neck, and head joints to get an overall costume height around 1.1–1.3 meters, then setting up arm and leg chains with proper joint roles and directions for an A-pose stance.

Defining leg and foot joints...

For the torso, I'm building a cardboard box part with flaps, tape strips, and a hand-drawn control panel featuring buttons, a dial, and a smiley screen, plus dark arm-hole tabs; the hips get blue shorts, and the head is a skin-toned sphere positioned at the top.

Now I'm figuring out the box helmet with a cutout face window framed by top, bottom, left, and right bars, revealing eyes, nose, mouth, and hair inside, with a small chin piece for the jaw. I'm working out the vertical placement: torso spans roughly 0.56 to 1.0, neck around 0.97-1.0, head centered near 1.1 with a kid-sized skull radius, and the helmet box centered just above that.

Adjusting for overlap, I settle on torso top at 0.98, helmet bottom opening at 1.02, helmet center at 1.18 with height 0.32 (spanning 1.02-1.34), head center at 1.14 with radius 0.1, and neck running 0.98-1.06, giving a total kid height around 1.34 with the box additions. Now I'm defining the helmet wall thickness and the front window opening coordinates relative to the face position.

Working out the window frame geometry: top bar, bottom bar, and side bars around the viewport, plus eye placement on the head sphere, nose, and jaw details including a lower jaw box and a dark mouth line for the smile.

I'm adding hair fringe visible through the helmet window, skipping hidden ears, then placing antenna rods with balls on top and toilet-paper-roll cylinders as side ear pieces wrapped in foil. For decoration I'm sketching crayon-style lightning bolts using an extruded shape on the helmet.

Now I'm defining the color palette for cardboard, tape, foil, and clothing tones, along with a helper function for placing boxes relative to bones in model space.

I also need a cylinder helper with a direction parameter for orienting parts like buttons, then I'm designing the torso front panel with colored buttons, a dial with a needle, and an SVG-textured screen showing a glowing green smiley face.

Now I'm adding vent slats, tape strips, and arm holes to the torso, then positioning A-pose arms with shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints plus skin-toned hand spheres.

Keeping the hands simple with palm boxes and a few finger boxes attached at the wrist joint, skipping cuffs, and giving the arms foil sleeve tubes at a constant radius.

Now I'm thinking through elbow detailing, considering crinkle-ring torus shapes placed along the arm chain to mimic foil wrinkles, and figuring out how to orient each torus so it faces tangent to the sweep direction using frame-based rotation.

For legs, I'm planning blue pants with cardboard knee pads and red sneakers rather than foil tubes, keeping it simple. I'll build the skeleton with hips as root, chest as child with neck/head/jaw chain, torso box on chest, and arm chains parenting to chest while leg chains parent to hips.

Now I'm setting up front/left directional conventions and mirroring arms and legs across sides with naming like hipL/hipR. For the helmet, I'm adding small foil side rolls as cylinders, an antenna rod with a ball tip attached to the head bone, and opened cardboard flaps on top of the helmet as thin angled boxes.

I'm reconsidering whether the flaps would clash with the antennas, so I'll skip extra torso flaps and instead focus on a neck collar, facial details like pink cheeks and freckled eyes with highlights, and a small backpack box on the back. I'm also thinking about adding a chest plaque labeled "BOT-9" rendered as SVG text, plus a wobbly hand-drawn marker effect for character.

Writing extrude code for a lightning bolt...

Now I'm working out the sneaker geometry: a red box body with a white sole box offset slightly below, positioning the ankle joint and chain so the shoe fully covers the foot.

For the hair, I'm layering a brown hemisphere cap over the head sphere plus small fringe boxes positioned just under the helmet's top bar so they stay visible through the window opening without clipping past it. I'm checking that eye placement on the head sphere aligns properly given its radius and center offset.

Now I'm placing the eyes with white sphere whites and darker pupils slightly recessed, then working out the jaw joint and lower jaw geometry, including a dark mouth interior box and a red lower lip piece to shape the smile.

I realize the chin and jaw may get hidden behind the helmet's window bottom bar, so I'm adjusting the window and bar vertical ranges and the helmet's overall bounds to keep the face visible from the front while still fitting above the torso.

Now I'm laying out the window frame itself: side walls, back wall, top bar, side bars, and bottom bar with their coordinates and thicknesses, then considering a small marker-drawn smile detail on the top bar.

Next I'm placing glowing yellow light circles at the top bar corners, then moving to the torso dimensions—depth, width, and height—figuring out where the shorts and helmet meet it, and sketching dark cylindrical arm-hole discs on either side where the sleeves will attach.

I'm adding a backpack box on the back with a dial and vertical foil cylinders, then setting the sweep chain to use a six-sided hexagonal cross-section instead of smooth circles. Finally I'm working out how to attach hand parts at the wrist joint using the arm's tip position as the reference point.

Defining a generic box helper for placing parts by bone, size, position, color, and rotation, then pulling in the glow kit module to finish the write-up.
